versions.short: The bill would extend through fiscal year 2031 and update a range of federal programs, run by the Health Resources and Services Administration, that help recruit, train, and keep people working or teaching in health careers. It would revise a loan repayment program for pediatric health specialists who agree to practice in areas short of them, requiring that direct clinical care make up at least half of their required service hours, widening the eligible specialties to include pediatric mental and behavioral health fields the agency deems appropriate, and allowing a focus on children enrolled in Medicaid. It would also authorize grants to states and health professions schools to support the nursing workforce through analysis, technical help, and best practices for easing nursing shortages. Finally, it would expand grants for recruiting young people into public health careers so that outreach includes middle school students, not only high school students.
